history-of-the-gatling-gun-detachment-fi: Lieutenant John Parker commanded the Gatling guns at Santiago in the Spanish-American War, and this is his unvarnished history of the detachment. He tells how the new weapons performed under fire — with refreshing honesty about what worked and what didn't. A valuable primary source on America's brief, decisive war.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agostino-barb: This 1913 reference article on Agostino Barbosa — the Portuguese master of canon law. Andrew Meehan praises his vast works. His commentaries guided bishops for a century. Lisbon's jurist served the universal Church. A canonist of the first rank. His Tractatus filled the bishops' shelves.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-de-esp: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Alonso de Espinosa — the historian of the Canary Islands. Ventura Fuentes notes his chronicle of the Guanches. His pages preserve a vanished people. The conquest's story lives in his book. A classic of the Atlantic isles.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arethusa: This 1913 reference article on Arethusa — the Syrian city, now a titular see. Thomas Shahan notes its Christian past. Its bishops graced the old councils. The Orontes guards its ruined site. A see of the eastern empire. Its walls recall the Seleucid kings.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aversa: A 1913 entry on Aversa — the Campanian diocese of the Norman town. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its bishops serve the fertile plain. The first Norman see in Italy. A diocese of the southern fields. Its mozzarella is famed through Italy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartholomew-o: This 1913 reference piece on Bartholomew of Edessa — a monk of the East. Romain Butin records what is known. The entry preserves his modest fame. The eastern calendars keep his name. A solitary of the ancient Church. His cell overlooked the Mesopotamian plain.

This 1913 reference article on Bartholomew of Pisa — the Franciscan of the Conformities. Paschal Robinson notes his famous book. His parallels likened Francis to Christ. The order debated his zeal. A friar of the strict observance. His book was the order's pride.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-basilissa: This 1913 reference article on Basilissa — a martyr of the early Church. Johann Peter Kirsch records what is known. The entry preserves her modest fame. The old calendars keep her name. A witness of the persecution age. Her name is blessed in the martyrologies.
